findings.problem: LedgerWorkflow uses status: String + is_validated: bool + is_sent: bool instead of enums/typestates. These primitives can represent contradictory states such as status="sent" with is_sent=false, or is_validated=true with status="draft". No constructor enforces invariants.
findings.failure_mode: Any code reading LedgerWorkflow must defensively check for contradictory field combinations. Business invariants (e.g. sent implies validated) are not enforced at compile time.
findings.fix: Replace status with a sealed enum (e.g. enum LedgerStatus { Draft, Validated, Sent }) and is_validated/is_sent with a typestate or derive them from status. Remove redundant bools.

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates LedgerWorkflow in-place (mut item) and returns the mutated struct. This is imperative-style state mutation disguised as a function. The function has no input validation and directly writes a magic string literal "sent".
findings.failure_mode: The caller can hold a reference to the original struct and observe inconsistent intermediate state. String literal "sent" bypasses the type system — any string can be assigned anywhere.
findings.fix: Use a pure transition: fn mark_sent(item: LedgerWorkflow) -> Result<LedgerWorkflow, TransitionError>. Validate preconditions (e.g. must be validated before sent), return a new struct, and use enum-typed status instead of string mutation.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain rules encoded. sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u6> is raw without a time type.
findings.failure_mode: Any code can construct a LedgerWorkflow with an empty id, invalid epoch, or malformed id string. Domain invariants (id format, non-zero timestamps) are unchecked.
findings.fix: Use newtypes: struct LedgerId(String) with a fallible constructor, and struct TimestampMs(u64) with non-zero validation at the boundary.

findings.problem: mark_sent uses "sent".to_string() which heap-allocates every call. The struct already owns a String for id, so every field is heap-allocated. No try_reserve or capacity awareness anywhere.
findings.failure_mode: Allocation failure (Err(Allocation)) is unhandled. In high-throughput or memory-constrained contexts, to_string() can fail silently or cause OOM.
findings.fix: Use enum-based status to eliminate string storage entirely. If strings are needed, use try_reserve at collection boundaries and handle Allocation errors.

findings.problem: No benchmarks exist for any performance claim. The crate has no benches/ directory, no criterion or built-in benchmark code, and no profiler or allocation tracking evidence.
findings.failure_mode: Without benchmarks, performance characteristics (especially around the to_string() allocation in mark_sent) are unverified and cannot be defended.
findings.fix: Add a criterion benchmark measuring mark_sent throughput and allocation count under realistic input sizes.

findings.problem: No flamegraph, perf, or sampler evidence exists. Hot paths are unidentified.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot confirm whether mark_sent is hot or cold. Optimization decisions are cargo-culted.
findings.fix: Run cargo flamegraph or perf on realistic workloads to identify hot paths.

findings.problem: No clippy, Miri, Kani, or other second-ring command evidence exists.
findings.failure_mode: Undefined behavior, data races, and proof gaps are unverified.
findings.fix: Run cargo clippy -- -D warnings and cargo miri test on any unsafe or concurrent code.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent throughput or allocation cost
no profiler/flamegraph evidence for hot-path identification
no allocation tracking (try_reserve, allocation error handling)
no second-ring command evidence (clippy, Miri, Kani, cargo test)
residual_risk: High. The domain model is fundamentally broken: illegal states are fully representable via String status + bool flags, business invariants are unenforceable, and mark_sent performs imperative mutation with magic string literals instead of typed typestate transitions. Without enum-based status and typestate enforcement, no amount of downstream checking can guarantee correctness. Static review only; no commands run.
